request.description:
POST /auth/login

CUSTOMERS: returns the user AND payload.tokens { accessToken, refreshToken }.
STAFF (admin / manager / pos_user): returns no tokens — an OTP is emailed and
the tokens come from POST /auth/verify-otp instead.

The test script saves a customer token into {{CUSTOMER_TOKEN}}.

POST /auth/reset-password

Flow: Forgot Password -> OTP emailed -> Reset Password WITH that OTP.

The otp field is mandatory. It is checked against the stored token, must not be
expired (10 minutes) and is cleared on use, so it cannot be replayed.

A successful reset signs the account out everywhere (session_invalidated_at) and
clears any failed-attempt lockout.

401 "Invalid or expired reset code" covers a wrong OTP, an expired OTP and an
unknown email - the message is deliberately identical so the endpoint cannot be
used to discover which addresses have accounts.

POST /auth/customer/logout

AUTH: authenticateCustomer — storefront headers (x-api-key + x-api-password)
PLUS a CUSTOMER Bearer token from POST /auth/login.
An admin/staff token is rejected with 403.

Stamps session_invalidated_at, so the JWT is genuinely dead immediately —
not merely forgotten by the client. Signs the account out on all devices.

Note: the admin POST /auth/logout only records last_logout_date and leaves
the token usable until it expires.

POST /auth/customer/forgot-password

AUTH: authenticateFrontend - storefront headers only (x-api-key + x-api-password).
No login required, and the endpoint only ever acts on role = customer, so a
storefront key can never drive a reset against a staff or admin account.

Emails a 6-digit reset code, valid for 10 minutes.

Always returns 200 with the same message, even for an unknown email, so the
endpoint cannot be used to discover which addresses have accounts.

STEP 1 of 3:  forgot-password -> verify-otp (optional) -> reset-password

POST /auth/customer/verify-otp

AUTH: authenticateFrontend - storefront headers only (x-api-key + x-api-password).
No login required, and the endpoint only ever acts on role = customer, so a
storefront key can never drive a reset against a staff or admin account.

OPTIONAL pre-check so the app can validate the code before showing the
new-password form. It does NOT consume the code - you can call it more than
once, and you still pass the same otp to reset-password afterwards.

200 -> { verified: true, email }
401 -> Invalid or expired code

Returns no tokens. (The admin POST /auth/verify-otp is a different thing: it is
the staff login step, it returns tokens, and it DOES consume the code.)

GET /reports/duration

Everything about one period in a single call — the whole report is a shareable link.

QUERY PARAMS
  period              Optional - Enum: today | yesterday | last_7_days | last_30_days |
                      this_month | last_month | this_year | custom   (default: custom)
  startDate           Required when period=custom - YYYY-MM-DD
  endDate             Required when period=custom - YYYY-MM-DD
  website_setting_id  Optional - number, scope to one store
  branch_id           Optional - number, scope to one branch
  channel             Optional - Enum: online_store | point_of_sale | admin
  status              Optional - Enum: booked | preparing | ready_for_pickup | shipped |
                      completed | cancelled | returned | refunded
  payment_status      Optional - Enum: pending | paid | failed | refunded
  include_orders      Optional - boolean (default true). false = totals only, much faster
  page                Optional - number (default 1)
  limit               Optional - number 1..200 (default 25)

RESPONSE payload
  period              { period, start_date, end_date, days }
  filters             the scope that was applied
  amounts             subtotal, discount, shipping, tax, total, paid, outstanding,
                      refunded, refund_count, gateway_fees, net_revenue
  orders_summary      orders_count, cancelled_count, cancelled_value, items_sold,
                      line_items, average_order_value, average_discount
  by_status           orders + total per order status
  by_payment_status   orders + total + paid per payment status
  by_payment_method   transactions + amount + gateway_fee per method
  by_channel          orders + total per channel
  by_delivery_type    orders + total + shipping_collected per delivery type
  coupons_used        code, times_used, discount_given
  daily               one row per day: orders, subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total, paid
  orders              full detail per order: customer, store, branch, coupon,
                      amounts{subtotal,discount,shipping,tax,total,paid,outstanding},
                      items[], payments[]

MONEY RULES
  total       = subtotal - discount + shipping + tax
  outstanding = total - paid
  net_revenue = paid - refunds - gateway fees

Cancelled orders are EXCLUDED from amounts and reported separately as
orders_summary.cancelled_count / cancelled_value. They still appear in by_status and in
the orders list, so the by_status totals will not sum to amounts.total.

request.description:
POST /reports/duration

The detailed period report with the FULL filter set. Same payload as
GET /reports/duration, which is the flat query-string shortcut of this endpoint.

Every key above is optional except startDate/endDate when period = custom.
Unknown keys inside filters are rejected with 422, so a typo never silently
widens the report.

Values accepting arrays behave as IN (...). For example:
  "status": ["completed", "shipped"]
  "payment_method": ["cash", "stripe"]

product_id / category_id match orders containing ANY item for that product or
category. payment_method matches orders having ANY captured payment by that method.

RESPONSE payload
  period              { period, start_date, end_date, days }
  filters             the filters that were applied (echoed back)
  sort                { sortBy, sortOrder }
  amounts             subtotal, discount, shipping, tax, total, paid, outstanding,
                      refunded, refund_count, gateway_fees, net_revenue
  orders_summary      orders_count, cancelled_count, cancelled_value, items_sold,
                      line_items, average_order_value, average_discount
  by_status           orders + total per order status
  by_payment_status   orders + total + paid per payment status
  by_payment_method   transactions + amount + gateway_fee per method
  by_channel          orders + total per channel
  by_delivery_type    orders + total + shipping_collected per delivery type
  coupons_used        code, times_used, discount_given
  daily               per-day: orders, subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total, paid
  orders              full detail: customer, store, branch, coupon,
                      amounts{subtotal,discount,shipping,tax,total,paid,outstanding},
                      items[], payments[]
  pagination          page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNext, hasPrev

MONEY RULES
  total       = subtotal - discount + shipping + tax
  outstanding = total - paid
  net_revenue = paid - refunds - gateway fees

Cancelled orders are EXCLUDED from amounts and reported separately as
orders_summary.cancelled_count / cancelled_value. They still appear in by_status and
in the orders list, so by_status totals will not sum to amounts.total.

POST /reports/duration/excel

The same report as POST /reports/duration, returned as a professional
multi-sheet .xlsx download. Accepts the IDENTICAL body and filter set.

SHEETS
  Summary       headline numbers + the filters that produced them
  Daily         day-by-day trend with a totals row
  Orders        one row per order with the full amount breakdown
  Order Items   one row per line item (what was actually sold)
  Payments      one row per payment taken
  Breakdowns    status / payment status / method / channel / delivery type
  Coupons       redemptions and discount given

Each sheet carries a branded banner (store name, title, period + filters +
generated timestamp), frozen headers, auto-filter, currency formatting from
the store's currency_symbol, zebra striping and a bold totals row.

NOTE ON page / limit
  They are ignored here. The export always pulls every matching order, so the
  Orders sheet can never disagree with the Summary sheet.

IN POSTMAN
  Use "Send and Download" to save the file, otherwise the binary is rendered
  as unreadable text in the response pane.
